about.title: Campbell Slip & Fall Claims
about.longDescription: Campbell's mix of retail centers along Hamilton Avenue, older apartment buildings, and busy sidewalks near downtown creates plenty of chances for a wet floor, cracked pavement, or poorly lit stairwell to cause a serious fall. Unlike a car crash, these cases hinge on proving the property owner or manager knew, or should have known, about the hazard and didn't fix it or warn people in time. That's why what happens in the hours after a fall matters so much: photos of the exact spot, the names of any witnesses, and a written incident report can make the difference later. Santa Clara County businesses often have surveillance cameras that record over footage within days or weeks, so preserving that video quickly is critical. We handle premises liability claims and work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover.

whyChoose.title: What Matters in a Campbell Premises Case

items.title: Proving Notice
items.desc: California law generally requires showing the property owner knew or reasonably should have known about the hazard and failed to address it. We can help gather maintenance logs, prior complaints, and inspection records to support that.

items.title: Racing the Clock on Evidence
items.desc: Surveillance footage from Campbell retailers or apartment complexes is often overwritten within days, and hazards get cleaned up fast. Acting early to request and preserve that video can be central to the claim.

items.title: Understanding Comparative Fault
items.desc: California uses pure comparative fault, so even if you're found partly responsible for a fall, you may still recover a reduced amount. We can help present the facts in a way that fairly accounts for shared responsibility.

items.question: How long do I have to file a slip and fall claim in Campbell?
items.answer: Generally, California gives you two years from the date of the fall to file a premises liability lawsuit. If the property involved is owned by a government entity, such as a city building or public sidewalk in Campbell, the deadline is much shorter and requires an early claim filing. Because these timelines vary, it's worth getting our input as soon as possible.

items.question: What if I fell in a store on Hamilton Avenue but didn't report it right away?
items.answer: Not reporting immediately doesn't automatically end your claim, but it can make proving what happened harder. Try to document the scene with photos, note any witnesses, and write down details while they're fresh, even after the fact. We can still help gather store records, video, and other evidence to reconstruct the incident.

items.question: Do I need a lawyer if the property owner's insurance already offered me money?
items.answer: Insurance companies often make early offers that don't reflect the full extent of medical treatment or long-term effects of an injury. It costs nothing to have us review the offer before you accept anything. We work on contingency, so there's no upfront cost to get a second opinion.
